newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS -Charts suggest bull run will pause.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS -Charts suggest bull run will pause.

text.p: International debt futures, revelling in a bullish uptrend, could be approaching near-term summits, technical analysts said on Tuesday.
However, analysts said there is nothing on the charts to say the bull run is over, merely that a pause is on the cards before another move upwards.

"We've seen a lot of frothy, speculative moves and it's time to look for a peak and a correction," said Anne Whitby, head of technical analysis at 4CAST in London. "It's not necessarily 'the' peak, but could well be "a' peak."
Since the end of October, most major bond futures have rallied strongly. Italian BTP futures have broken through previous record highs, and have set a new one at 128.38.
German Bund futures have set their sights on doing the same at the 101.48 all-time high, while French notionnel futures have set new highs for the December contract.
U.S. Treasury futures have reached their highest levels since February, rallying from a low of 110-00 on October 25 to a high of 115-15 on November 15.

Even given the recent rises, analysts said there is still room to manoeuvre upwards. Phillip Gardiner, fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London, said Bunds lead the pack with a further two points of upside potential.
He said December Bund futures had rallied four points from a low of 95.90 on September 3 to a high of 99.94 on October 9, before holding steady for a period of four weeks.
"I would look for the second bull run to be equal in length to the first," he said. "We've already had about two points of it, so another two looks possible."
Rising momentum indicators in the notionnel suggest the rise could be extended by 1-1/2 points, according to Gardiner. He also cited a target of 118-00 for T-bond futures.
But the speed of the rise means support for the contracts could be limited if they start to fall, analysts said.

"Short-term all bond futures look capable of higher levels but if I was a long term player I would be wondering quite how much more was left in it and would be thinking of positioning myself," said David Wood, an independent technical analyst based near London.
Whitby said British gilts could prove a shelter from a correction in bond markets, as the futures have failed to make moves of the same magnitude as their counterparts.

Gilts have been dogged by domestic worries, and have not set new contract highs since 111-17 in mid-October. Also, T-bond futures have not challenged the 120-00 highs from late December 1995/early January 1996.
"Gilts are not overbought and have underperformed recently in a sideways range, while T-bonds are stuck below the 120-00 top," said Whitby. "The U.S. and the UK look the least dangerous short-term."
Whitby said short-dated bond contracts suggested that interest rates were not going to drop much further and were bottoming out.

"That is a negative factor for bonds, and gives a strong risk that the markets are at important peaks," she said. "If the U.S. breaks back sharply it will give the European markets pause for thought."
But Gardiner said he remained bullish on U.S. Treasuries, with the market still technically correcting the major decline from the start of the year.
"T-bond futures would have to get below 111-28, the October 4 high before I would turn bearish," he said. "But I'd be neutral if it fell below 113-22, the November 8 low."
